summary: 60-foot steel tower built 1916 on Hardwood Mountain, Somerset County, Maine; cab gone per Forest Lookouts list; 2016 chapter visit found it standing; FFLOS register says gone.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts list shows it standing with the cab no longer in place (asterisk); the 2016 chapter report found the structure standing; the FFLOS register entry, dated 2008, says it is no longer standing. We found no date for the cab's removal.

visit.trail_note: Very remote tower on the Canadian border; the 2016 chapter report describes a trip in by a chapter friend. No public access statement found.

events.note: Newspaper of November 1, 1916 says the big lookout tower was built that year on Hardwood Mountain in Township 9, R18; 1916 forest commissioner's report describes a new lookout station there
Forest Lookouts quotes the 1920 inventory listing a 60-foot steel tower
Registered September 15, 2008 as US 107, ME 33; nominated by Henry Isenberg; register description says the tower is no longer standing
Maine chapter 2016 survey: tower had long been thought not standing; a trip in by a chapter friend found it standing; listed as a tower change

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts list shows the tower standing with the cab no longer in place. The 2016 chapter report found the tower standing. The FFLOS register entry dates from 2008, before that visit, so we keep standing with the cab gone.

notes_for_editor: Status: the register (firetower.org, registered 2008) says no longer standing; the 2016 chapter report and the Forest Lookouts list say standing, with the cab gone per the list's asterisk legend. Cab removal date not found. The 1916 sources name W.F. Hinckley (newspaper) and W.H. Hinckley (report); we did not decide whether they are the same man. A web search summary mentioned a 2020 'Structure Only - No Cab' entry on firelookout.org and a 1923 Maine State Archives panorama map, and it gave a 75-foot height; none of those pages could be read (firelookout.org/lookouts/me/me.htm returned 404), so none is used. Height is 60 feet per the 1920 inventory quoted by Forest Lookouts, so the brief's 18.3 m stands. Access: no public-access statement found; the only access fact is the 2016 'trip in'. No photos added.
